title: Tool Helmsman: adaptive routing, streamed tool emission, and reentrancy throttle
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We support multi-tool chains where the LLM can call external tools (search, DB, calculators) and then incorporate results back into subsequent calls. Existing implementations either (a) eagerly inject full tool payloads into the model context which inflates token cost and increases latency, or (b) stream tool outputs without reliable provenance, making troubleshooting and deterministic replay hard. Additionally, compatibility support for legacy function-calling APIs is fragmented across the runtime, causing duplicated adapters and edge-case bugs.

Goal: Implement a unified executor component (Tool Helmsman) that: 1) supports adaptive routing of tool calls to the best endpoint variant (hosted/dedicated/private) by policy; 2) streams partial tool outputs back to the client while also persisting compact provenance for deterministic replays; 3) injects tool results into the LLM context using a token-efficient, schema-driven hybrid (summary + optional detail-on-demand); 4) prevents runaway recursion/looping from chained tool calls via a reentrancy throttle algorithm; and 5) provides a compatibility layer that translates legacy function-calling payloads into the new structured-output contract.

Scope & Acceptance Criteria:
- Design and land a new runtime component Tool Helmsman that sits between the orchestration layer and tool adapters.
- API: add experimental executor flag `helm: true` to route sessions through the component. Flag default off.
- Streaming: partial tool outputs must be streamable to the client within 150ms of first byte from the tool adapter for 95% of requests in local load tests.
- Provenance: every streamed fragment must include a compact provenance token (epoch-hash + adapter-id + short-offset) persisted to the request trace. Provenance size must be <= 128 bytes per fragment.
- Injection policy: introduce two injection modes: `summary-first` (default) and `pass-through`. `summary-first` injects a 1-2 sentence canonical summary plus compact pointer to full payload; `pass-through` injects full payloads but only when explicitly allowed by a per-route config.
- Compatibility: implement an adapter that maps legacy function-calling fields (name, arguments, typed results) to the structured output schema and round-trips without semantic drift for our test corpus (100+ samples).
- Safety: reentrancy throttle prohibits more than N tool-invocation hops within a sliding window (configurable per-customer). Default N=6. When throttle triggers, the executor should produce a non-retryable structured error object and emit a metric and trace event.
- Telemetry: emit metrics for stream latency, provenance size distribution, injection mode usage, throttle events, and compatibility-mapping failures.
- Tests: unit tests for mapping, integration smoke for streaming + provenance, load test demonstrating <150ms first-byte for partial streams under 50 RPS, and fuzz tests to ensure no unbounded context growth.

Design Notes & Trade-offs:
- Provenance format: using epoch-hash + adapter id + offset keeps per-fragment size small and avoids storing full content in traces. Trade-off: requires service-side compact store for reconstructing fragments during replay. We will first implement reconstruction tooling for SRE and hold full content in short-term object storage (7 days) to avoid long-term storage costs.
- Summary-first injection reduces token cost but can cause lossy information for downstream tools. We mitigate with on-demand detail retrieval: downstream tool adapters can request full payloads via the provenance token. This adds an extra RTT but keeps common-case cost down.
- Reentrancy throttle vs semantic loop detection: throttle is simple and deterministic but can block valid deep pipelines. Longer term we want a semantic loop detector (cycle detection on call graph) but that needs heavier static/model analysis and will be a follow-up.
- Compatibility layer will intentionally accept some legacy oddities (e.g., stringified JSON args) and normalize them. We will maintain an allowlist of legacy fields to avoid surprising behavior changes for older customers.

Implementation Plan:
1) Prototype (Week 1-2): implement Tool Helmsman internal API, local adapter shim, minimal provenance token format, and summary-first injection. Quick demo with search and calculator adapters.
2) Integration (Week 3): add streaming plumbing to SDKs and route partial fragments through the HTTP/streaming path with provenance headers. Implement legacy adapter to map function-calling examples.
3) Safety & Telemetry (Week 4): implement reentrancy throttle, emit metrics/traces, add feature flag.
4) Tests & Load (Week 5): run the load tests, craft fuzz cases, and add integration tests to CI.
5) Canary & Rollout (Week 6-7): enable for internal customers and a small external canary; watch metrics for stream latency and throttle hits.

APIs and Configs (proposal):
- executor.start(session, helm=true|false, injection_mode=summary-first|pass-through)
- per-route config: helm: {enabled: bool, max_hops: int, allowed_pass_through: bool}
- fragment headers (stream): X-Helm-Provenance: <epoch-hash>;<adapter-id>;<offset>

Open Questions:
- Default max_hops: should this be 6 or 8? PM prefers 6 for customer safety; infra recommends 8 for complex workflows. Decision: start with 6 and surface an admin knob.
- Provenance retention window: 7 days vs 30 days. Cost analysis favors 7 days; compliance may require 30 for some customers. We'll make retention configurable per-customer.
- Backpressure: how to reconcile adapter backpressure with streaming guarantees for LM contexts. Proposed: Helmsman will buffer up to M fragments (M=8) per-request and apply early-drop policy for non-critical adapters.

Rollout & Monitoring:
- Feature flag `helm_executor` guarded by per-tenant allowlist.
- Dashboards: stream-first-byte latency, average provenance size, throttle events per-tenant, compatibility-mapper error rate.
- Alerting: throttle rate > 0.5% of requests for >5 min triggers oncall. Compatibility-mapper error rate > 1% for canary triggers engineering review.

Acceptance / Definition of Done:
- All acceptance criteria above implemented, code reviewed, and merged behind feature flag.
- Integration tests pass in CI and internal canary shows stable stream latency and expected throttle behavior.
- Docs: PRD + design doc linked, API docs updated, and SDK example for summary-first + provenance retrieval added.

Links and Artifacts:
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Tool+Helmsman+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921
- Streaming SDK example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/main/helm-examples

Follow-ups:
- Semantic loop/cycle detection (future ticket).
- Per-customer provenance retention policy + billing impact.
- UI in Console to visualize provenance fragments and replay requests for SRE/CS.
